subject: math
title: Measurement Conversions
seo_title: Grade 5 Measurement Conversion Worksheets: Convert to Larger Units with Decimals and Fractions, Multi-Step Problems
standard_text: Convert among different-sized standard measurement units within a given measurement system (e.g., convert 5 cm to 0.05 m), and use these conversions in solving multi-step, real world problems.
meta_desc: Free Grade 5 measurement conversion worksheets: convert both ways between km, m, cm, mm, kg, g, L, mL, miles, yards, feet, inches, pounds, ounces, tons, cups, pints, quarts, gallons and time, with decimals (5 cm = 0.05 m) and fractions (30 in = 2½ ft). Compare measurements and solve multi-step word problems. 100 practice questions with step-by-step answers.
key_big: To a bigger unit, divide. To a smaller unit, multiply.
key_sub: 1 m = 100 cm, so 250 cm = 250 ÷ 100 = 2.5 m and 5 cm = 0.05 m. A leftover becomes a fraction: 30 in = 2 ft 6 in = 2½ ft, and 90 min = 1½ hr = 1 hr 30 min (not 1 hr 50 min).
body_html:
The big idea

To change to a bigger unit, divide: you need fewer of the big units. To change to a smaller unit, multiply: you need more of the small units.

Two ways

3 m = ☐ cm   and   250 cm = ☐ m

1 m = 100 cm. To centimeters (smaller): 3 × 100 = 300. To meters (bigger): 250 ÷ 100 = 2.5.

Answer: 300 cm and 2.5 m

Metric units: powers of 10

Metric units go up by 10, 100 or 1,000, so you only move the decimal point.

FactTo the smaller unitTo the bigger unit
1 km = 1,000 m× 1,000: point 3 places right÷ 1,000: point 3 places left
1 m = 100 cm× 100: point 2 places right÷ 100: point 2 places left
1 cm = 10 mm× 10: point 1 place right÷ 10: point 1 place left
1 kg = 1,000 g0.75 kg = 750 g750 g = 0.75 kg
1 L = 1,000 mL1.2 L = 1,200 mL600 mL = 0.6 L

Customary units and time

These do not go up by 10, so learn each number.

MeasureFacts
Length1 ft = 12 in   1 yd = 3 ft = 36 in   1 mi = 5,280 ft
Weight1 lb = 16 oz   1 ton = 2,000 lb
Capacity1 pt = 2 cups   1 qt = 2 pt   1 gal = 4 qt
Time1 min = 60 sec   1 hr = 60 min   1 day = 24 hr   1 week = 7 days

Fractions, decimals and mixed units

When the division has a remainder, write the leftover as a fraction of the big unit, or keep it as a mixed unit.

Inches to feet

30 in = ☐ ft

30 ÷ 12 = 2 R6. 6 inches is 612 = 12 of a foot.

Answer: 2 12 ft, or 2 ft 6 in

Minutes to hours

90 min = ☐ hr

90 ÷ 60 = 1 R30. 30 minutes is 3060 = 12 of an hour.

Answer: 1 12 hr = 1.5 hr = 1 hr 30 min

Multi-step problems

First change all the measurements to one unit. Then solve. Change the answer to the unit the question asks for.

Example

5 bags of apples weigh 900 g each. What is the total mass in kilograms?

Step 1: 5 × 900 = 4,500 g. Step 2: 4,500 ÷ 1,000 = 4.5.

Answer: 4.5 kg

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Multiplying to get a bigger unit (250 cm = 25,000 m)To a bigger unit, divide: 250 ÷ 100 = 2.5 m
Moving the point the wrong number of places (5 cm = 0.5 m)÷ 100 moves it 2 places: 5 cm = 0.05 m
Using 10 or 100 for customary units (30 in = 3 ft)1 ft = 12 in, so 30 in = 2 12 ft
Writing a mixed unit as a decimal (90 min = 1.3 hr)1 hr 30 min = 1 12 hr = 1.5 hr
Mixing up pints and quarts (3 qt = 12 pt)1 qt = 2 pt, so 3 qt = 6 pt. 4 qt = 1 gal

faq.q: How do you convert smaller units to larger units in 5th grade?
faq.a: Divide by the number of small units in 1 large unit. For example, 1 m = 100 cm, so 250 cm = 250 ÷ 100 = 2.5 m.

faq.q: How do you convert 5 cm to meters?
faq.a: Divide by 100, which moves the decimal point 2 places to the left: 5 cm = 0.05 m. A common mistake is 0.5 m, which moves it only 1 place.

faq.q: How many cups, pints and quarts are in a gallon?
faq.a: 1 gallon = 4 quarts = 8 pints = 16 cups, because 1 quart = 2 pints and 1 pint = 2 cups.

It is the Common Core Grade 5 standard for converting between bigger and smaller units in the same measurement system, such as 5 cm = 0.05 m, and using these conversions to solve multi-step real-world problems.

sets.title: Metric units: multiply or divide by 10, 100, 1,000

items.e: 1 km = 1,000 m. Kilometers are bigger than meters, so there will be more meters: multiply by 1,000. The point moves 3 places right: 3.5 × 1,000 = 3,500, so 3.5 km = 3,500 m.
1 m = 100 cm. Meters are bigger than centimeters, so there will be more centimeters: multiply by 100. The point moves 2 places right: 4.2 × 100 = 420, so 4.2 m = 420 cm.
1 kg = 1,000 g. Kilograms are bigger than grams, so there will be more grams: multiply by 1,000. The point moves 3 places right: 0.6 × 1,000 = 600, so 0.6 kg = 600 g.
1 L = 1,000 mL. Liters are bigger than milliliters, so there will be more milliliters: multiply by 1,000. The point moves 3 places right: 1.25 × 1,000 = 1,250, so 1.25 L = 1,250 mL.
1 m = 100 cm. Meters are bigger than centimeters, so there will be fewer of them: divide by 100. The point moves 2 places left: 250 ÷ 100 = 2.5, so 250 cm = 2.5 m.
1 m = 100 cm. Meters are bigger than centimeters, so there will be fewer of them: divide by 100. The point moves 2 places left: 5 ÷ 100 = 0.05, so 5 cm = 0.05 m.
1 kg = 1,000 g. Kilograms are bigger than grams, so there will be fewer of them: divide by 1,000. The point moves 3 places left: 750 ÷ 1,000 = 0.75, so 750 g = 0.75 kg.
1 km = 1,000 m. Kilometers are bigger than meters, so there will be fewer of them: divide by 1,000. The point moves 3 places left: 3,200 ÷ 1,000 = 3.2, so 3,200 m = 3.2 km.

items.q: To change 2,400 g to kilograms, what do you do?
items.e: 1 kg = 1,000 g. A kilogram is bigger than a gram, so there will be fewer kilograms: divide by 1,000. 2,400 ÷ 1,000 = 2.4, so 2,400 g = 2.4 kg.

items.q: What number goes in the ? box?
items.e: 1 m = 100 cm, so every number on the right is the left number ÷ 100. 275 ÷ 100 = 2.75 (the point moves 2 places left).
1 cm = 10 mm. Centimeters are bigger than millimeters, so there will be more millimeters: multiply by 10. The point moves 1 place right: 0.8 × 10 = 8, so 0.8 cm = 8 mm.
1 m = 1,000 mm. Meters are bigger than millimeters, so there will be more millimeters: multiply by 1,000. The point moves 3 places right: 2.75 × 1,000 = 2,750, so 2.75 m = 2,750 mm.
1 m = 100 cm. Meters are bigger than centimeters, so there will be more centimeters: multiply by 100. The point moves 2 places right: 0.4 × 100 = 40, so 0.4 m = 40 cm.

items.q: You change 6.8 m to centimeters. How does the decimal point move?
items.e: 1 m = 100 cm, so multiply by 100. 100 has 2 zeros, and multiplying makes the number bigger, so the point moves 2 places right: 6.8 m = 680 cm.
1 L = 1,000 mL. Liters are bigger than milliliters, so there will be fewer of them: divide by 1,000. The point moves 3 places left: 600 ÷ 1,000 = 0.6, so 600 mL = 0.6 L.
1 cm = 10 mm. Centimeters are bigger than millimeters, so there will be fewer of them: divide by 10. The point moves 1 place left: 45 ÷ 10 = 4.5, so 45 mm = 4.5 cm.
1 kg = 1,000 g. Kilograms are bigger than grams, so there will be fewer of them: divide by 1,000. The point moves 3 places left: 80 ÷ 1,000 = 0.08, so 80 g = 0.08 kg.
1 L = 1,000 mL. Liters are bigger than milliliters, so there will be fewer of them: divide by 1,000. The point moves 3 places left: 1,500 ÷ 1,000 = 1.5, so 1,500 mL = 1.5 L.
1 m = 1,000 mm. Meters are bigger than millimeters, so there will be fewer of them: divide by 1,000. The point moves 3 places left: 350 ÷ 1,000 = 0.35, so 350 mm = 0.35 m.

items.q: What number goes in the ? box?
items.e: 1 kg = 1,000 g, so every number on the right is the left number ÷ 1,000. 1,750 ÷ 1,000 = 1.75 (the point moves 3 places left).

sets.title: Customary length and weight: fractions and mixed units

items.e: 1 yd = 3 ft. Feet are smaller, so multiply: 4 × 3 = 12, so 4 yd = 12 ft. (48 uses 12, the inches in a foot.)
1 yd = 3 ft. Yards are bigger, so divide: 9 ÷ 3 = 3, so 9 ft = 3 yd. (27 multiplies instead of dividing.)

items.q: Convert. 3 12 ft = ☐ in
items.e: 1 ft = 12 in. Inches are smaller, so multiply: 3 × 12 = 36, and 12 of 12 = 6. 36 + 6 = 42, so 3 12 ft = 42 in. (36 in forgets the half foot, and 35 in uses 10 instead of 12.)
1 mi = 5,280 ft. Feet are smaller, so multiply: 2 × 5,280 = 10,560, so 2 mi = 10,560 ft. (2,640 divides instead of multiplying, and 3,520 is the number of yards in 2 miles.)

1 ft = 12 in. Feet are bigger, so divide: 30 ÷ 12 = 2 R6. The 6 inches left over are 612 of a foot = 12, so 30 in = 2 12 ft. (3 ft divides by 10. 2.6 ft is a mistake for 2 ft 6 in: 6 inches is half a foot, not 0.6 of a foot.)

1 lb = 16 oz. Pounds are bigger, so divide: 40 ÷ 16 = 2 R8. The 8 ounces left over are 816 of a pound = 12, so 40 oz = 2 12 lb. (4 lb divides by 10. 2.8 lb is a mistake for 2 lb 8 oz: 8 oz is half a pound, not 0.8 of a pound.)
1 ft = 12 in, so 4 ft = 4 × 12 = 48 in. Add the leftover inches: 48 + 9 = 57 in. (49 in uses 10 instead of 12, and 48 in forgets the 9 inches.)
1 lb = 16 oz. Pounds are bigger, so divide: 8 ÷ 16. 8 oz is 816 of a pound = 12, so 8 oz = 12 lb. (2 lb divides 16 by 8, the wrong way round.)
1 ft = 12 in. Feet are bigger, so divide: 18 ÷ 12 = 1 R6. The 6 inches left over are 612 of a foot = 12, so 18 in = 1 12 ft. (6 ft divides by 3, the feet in a yard.)

items.q: Convert. 2 34 lb = ☐ oz
items.e: 1 lb = 16 oz. Ounces are smaller, so multiply: 2 × 16 = 32, and 34 of 16 = 12. 32 + 12 = 44, so 2 34 lb = 44 oz. (32 oz forgets the 34 pound, and 27.5 oz uses 10 instead of 16.)
1 lb = 16 oz, so 6 lb = 6 × 16 = 96 oz. Add the leftover ounces: 96 + 5 = 101 oz. (65 oz writes the digits side by side, and 77 oz uses 12 instead of 16.)
1 ton = 2,000 lb. Tons are bigger, so divide: 4,000 ÷ 2,000 = 2, so 4,000 lb = 2 tons. (4 tons divides by 1,000, and 250 tons divides by 16, the ounces in a pound.)

items.q: Convert. 1 12 tons = ☐ lb
items.e: 1 ton = 2,000 lb. Pounds are smaller, so multiply: 1 × 2,000 = 2,000, and 12 of 2,000 = 1,000. 2,000 + 1,000 = 3,000, so 1 12 tons = 3,000 lb. (1,500 lb uses 1,000 instead of 2,000, and 24 lb uses 16, the ounces in a pound.)
1 yd = 3 ft, so 1 yd 2 ft = 3 + 2 = 5 ft. 1 ft = 12 in, so 5 ft = 5 × 12 = 60 in. (36 in forgets the 2 feet, and 38 in adds 2 inches instead of 2 feet.)
1 ft = 12 in. 42 ÷ 12 = 3 R6: 3 whole feet and 6 inches left over, so 42 in = 3 ft 6 in. Check: 36 + 6 = 42. (4 ft 2 in divides by 10.)
1 mi = 5,280 ft. Miles are bigger, so divide: 2,640 ÷ 5,280. 2,640 is half of 5,280, so 2,640 ft = 12 mi. (2 mi divides 5,280 by 2,640, the wrong way round. 2.64 mi divides by 1,000.)

items.q: Convert. 14 mi = ☐ ft
items.e: 1 mi = 5,280 ft. Feet are smaller, so multiply: 14 of 5,280 = 5,280 ÷ 4 = 1,320, so 14 mi = 1,320 ft. (21,120 multiplies by 4 instead of finding one fourth, and 2,640 ft is half a mile.)

items.q: Convert. 3 13 yd = ☐ ft
items.e: 1 yd = 3 ft. Feet are smaller, so multiply: 3 × 3 = 9, and 13 of 3 = 1. 9 + 1 = 10, so 3 13 yd = 10 ft. (9 13 ft forgets to multiply the 13 by 3.)
1 lb = 16 oz. 52 ÷ 16 = 3 R4: 3 whole pounds and 4 ounces left over, so 52 oz = 3 lb 4 oz. Check: 48 + 4 = 52. (5 lb 2 oz divides by 10, and 4 lb 4 oz uses 12 instead of 16.)

1 ft = 12 in. Feet are bigger, so divide: 75 ÷ 12 = 6 R3. The 3 inches left over are 312 of a foot = 14, so 75 in = 6 14 ft. (7.5 ft divides by 10. 6.3 ft and 6 13 ft both treat the 3 leftover inches as 3 tenths or 1 third of a foot.)

sets.title: Capacity and time: cups, pints, quarts, gallons, hours

items.e: 1 qt = 2 pt. Pints are smaller, so multiply: 3 × 2 = 6, so 3 qt = 6 pt. (12 pt uses 4, the quarts in a gallon, and 1 12 pt divides instead of multiplying.)
1 pt = 2 cups. Pints are bigger, so divide: 6 ÷ 2 = 3, so 6 cups = 3 pt. (12 pt multiplies instead of dividing, and 1 12 pt divides by 4, the cups in a quart.)
1 gal = 4 qt. Quarts are smaller, so multiply: 2 × 4 = 8, so 2 gal = 8 qt. (4 qt multiplies by 2 instead of 4, and 16 is the number of pints in 2 gallons.)
1 gal = 4 qt. Gallons are bigger, so divide: 12 ÷ 4 = 3, so 12 qt = 3 gal. (48 gal multiplies instead of dividing, and 6 gal divides by 2, the pints in a quart.)

items.q: Convert. 12 gal = ☐ cups
items.e: 1 gal = 4 qt and 1 qt = 4 cups, so 1 gal = 16 cups. Half of 16 is 8 cups. (2 cups is the number of quarts in 12 gallon, and 32 cups doubles instead of halving.)
1 gal = 4 qt, so 3 gal = 3 × 4 = 12 qt. Add the leftover quarts: 12 + 2 = 14 qt. (32 qt writes the digits side by side, and 8 qt uses 2 instead of 4.)
1 qt = 2 pt. Quarts are bigger, so divide: 5 ÷ 2 = 2 R1. The 1 pint left over is 12 of a quart, so 5 pt = 2 12 qt. (1 14 qt divides by 4, and 2 14 qt treats the leftover pint as 14 quart.)

1 gal = 4 qt. Gallons are bigger, so divide: 10 ÷ 4 = 2 R2. The 2 quarts left over are 24 of a gallon = 12, so 10 qt = 2 12 gal. (2.2 gal is a mistake for 2 gal 2 qt: 2 quarts is half a gallon, not 0.2 of a gallon.)

items.q: What number goes in the ? box?
items.e: 1 gal = 4 qt, so every number on the right is the left number ÷ 4. 10 ÷ 4 = 2 R2, and 2 quarts is 24 = 12 gallon, so the answer is 2 12. (5 divides by 2, and 2.2 is a mistake for 2 gal 2 qt.)
1 qt = 4 cups. Quarts are bigger, so divide: 3 ÷ 4. 3 cups is 34 of a quart, so 3 cups = 34 qt. (12 qt multiplies instead of dividing, and 1 12 qt divides by 2, the cups in a pint.)

1 hr = 60 min. Hours are bigger, so divide: 90 ÷ 60 = 1 R30. The 30 minutes left over are 3060 of an hour = 12, so 90 min = 1 12 hr. (9 hr divides by 10 and 0.9 hr divides by 100. 1.3 hr is a mistake for 1 hr 30 min.)

items.q: Which is the same as 1.5 hours?
items.e: 1.5 hours is 1 hour and half an hour. Half of 60 minutes is 30 minutes, so 1.5 hr = 1 hr 30 min = 90 min. The .5 means one half, not 50 minutes: an hour has 60 minutes, not 100.
1 hr = 60 min. Hours are bigger, so divide: 45 ÷ 60. 45 min is 4560 of an hour = 34, so 45 min = 34 hr. (0.45 hr divides by 100, and 2,700 hr multiplies instead of dividing.)
0.25 = 14. 1 hr = 60 min, and 14 of 60 = 60 ÷ 4 = 15 min. (25 min reads the decimal as minutes, and 240 min divides 60 by 0.25.)

1 min = 60 sec. Minutes are bigger, so divide: 150 ÷ 60 = 2 R30. The 30 seconds left over are 3060 of a minute = 12, so 150 sec = 2 12 min. (1.5 min divides by 100. 2.3 min is a mistake for 2 min 30 sec.)

items.q: Convert. 2 14 hr = ☐ min
items.e: 1 hr = 60 min. Minutes are smaller, so multiply: 2 × 60 = 120, and 14 of 60 = 15. 120 + 15 = 135, so 2 14 hr = 135 min. (225 min uses 100 instead of 60, and 120 min forgets the 14 hour.)

items.q: What number goes in the ? box?
items.e: 1 hr = 60 min, so every number on the right is the left number ÷ 60. 105 ÷ 60 = 1 R45, and 45 minutes is 4560 = 34 of an hour, so the answer is 1 34. (1.05 divides by 100, 10 12 divides by 10, and 6,300 multiplies instead of dividing.)
1 day = 24 hr. Days are bigger, so divide: 36 ÷ 24 = 1 R12. The 12 hours left over are 1224 of a day = 12, so 36 hr = 1 12 days. (3 days divides by 12. 1.2 days is a mistake for 1 day 12 hours.)
1 hr = 60 min. 200 ÷ 60 = 3 R20: 3 whole hours and 20 minutes left over, so 200 min = 3 hr 20 min. Check: 180 + 20 = 200. (2 hr uses 100 minutes in an hour.)

items.q: Which is the same as 3 14 hours?
items.e: 14 of an hour is 60 ÷ 4 = 15 minutes, so 3 14 hr = 3 hr 15 min = 195 min. (3 hr 25 min reads 14 as 0.25, and 3 hr 4 min uses the 4 from the fraction.)
Change everything to centimeters: 1.2 m = 120 cm, 1,150 mm = 115 cm and 1 m 25 cm = 125 cm. In order: 125 cm, 120 cm, 115 cm, 98 cm. So the answer is 1 m 25 cm.
Change everything to grams: 0.8 kg = 800 g and 0.09 kg = 90 g (not 900 g). In order: 820 g, 800 g, 750 g, 90 g. So the answer is 820 g.
Change everything to milliliters: 0.5 L = 500 mL and 0.05 L = 50 mL. In order: 50 mL, 120 mL, 450 mL, 500 mL. So the answer is 0.05 L.
Change everything to grams: 1.05 kg = 1,050 g and 1.5 kg = 1,500 g. In order: 1,010 g, 1,050 g, 1,100 g, 1,500 g. So the answer is 1,010 g.

c: 2 12 ft = 2 ft 5 in
items.e: 2 ft = 24 in, and 12 ft = 6 in, so 2 12 ft = 30 in. Half a foot is 6 inches, not 5, and 30 in is not 3 ft because 1 ft = 12 in, not 10.

items.q: Which list goes from least to greatest?
items.e: Change them to the same unit: 0.5 m = 500 mm and 6 cm = 60 mm, and 8 < 60 < 500. The biggest number is not always the longest length. So the order is 8 mm, 6 cm, 0.5 m.
Change everything to inches: 2 12 ft = 24 + 6 = 30 in, 1 yd = 36 in and 2 ft 8 in = 24 + 8 = 32 in. In order: 36 in, 32 in, 30 in, 28 in. So the answer is 1 yd.
Change everything to ounces: 2 14 lb = 32 + 4 = 36 oz and 2 lb 5 oz = 32 + 5 = 37 oz. In order: 37 oz, 36 oz, 35 oz, 34 oz. So the answer is 2 lb 5 oz.
2.5 hr = 2 hours and half an hour = 120 + 30 = 150 min. The .5 is one half of 60 minutes, which is 30 minutes, not 50.
Change everything to cups: 3 qt = 12 cups, 5 pt = 10 cups and 1 gal = 16 cups. In order: 16 cups, 14 cups, 12 cups, 10 cups. So the answer is 1 gal.

items.q: Which is the longest amount of time?
items.e: Change everything to minutes: 1 12 hr = 90 min, 1 hr 35 min = 95 min and 1 34 hr = 60 + 45 = 105 min. In order: 105 min, 100 min, 95 min, 90 min. So the answer is 1 34 hr.
1 qt = 2 pt, so 3 pt is more than 1 qt: 3 pt > 1 qt. 3 pt is only 38 gal, and 2 qt = 8 cups, which is more than 6 cups.

items.q: Which list goes from least to greatest?
c: 1 ft 1 in, 16 in, 1 14 ft
16 in, 1 14 ft, 1 ft 1 in
1 ft 1 in, 1 14 ft, 16 in
1 14 ft, 1 ft 1 in, 16 in
items.e: Change them to the same unit: 1 14 ft = 12 + 3 = 15 in and 1 ft 1 in = 12 + 1 = 13 in, and 13 < 15 < 16. So the order is 1 ft 1 in, 1 14 ft, 16 in.
1 lb = 16 oz. 14 of 16 is 4, so 34 of 16 is 3 × 4 = 12. 34 lb = 12 oz, which is less than 1 lb.

items.q: Which is NOT equal to 2 qt?
items.e: 1 qt = 2 pt = 4 cups, so 2 qt = 4 pt = 8 cups. 1 gal = 4 qt, so 12 gal = 2 qt too. 6 cups is only 1 12 qt.

items.q: Which list goes from greatest to least?
c: 2 hr, 1 34 hr, 110 min
1 34 hr, 110 min, 2 hr
110 min, 2 hr, 1 34 hr
2 hr, 110 min, 1 34 hr
items.e: Change them to the same unit: 2 hr = 120 min and 1 34 hr = 60 + 45 = 105 min, and 120 > 110 > 105. So the order is 2 hr, 110 min, 1 34 hr.
Change everything to feet: 12 mi = 5,280 ÷ 2 = 2,640 ft and 900 yd = 900 × 3 = 2,700 ft. In order: 2,500 ft, 2,640 ft, 2,700 ft, 3,000 ft. So the answer is 2,500 ft.

items.q: Which is NOT equal to 1.5 m?
items.e: 1.5 m = 150 cm = 1,500 mm = 1 m 50 cm. 1 m 5 cm is only 105 cm: the .5 means 50 cm, not 5 cm.

items.q: Ava has a ribbon 2 m long. She cuts it into pieces that are 25 cm long. How many pieces does she get?
items.e: Use the same unit: 2 m = 200 cm. 200 ÷ 25 = 8 pieces. (80 uses 1 m = 1,000 cm, 50 multiplies 2 × 25, and 4 uses only 1 m.)

items.q: A store sells rice in 750 g bags. What is the total mass of 6 bags in kilograms?
items.e: Step 1: 6 × 750 = 4,500 g. Step 2: 1 kg = 1,000 g, so divide: 4,500 ÷ 1,000 = 4.5 kg. (4,500 kg forgets to convert.)

items.q: A track is 400 m around. Omar runs 12 laps. How many kilometers does he run?
A snail moves 5 cm each minute. How many meters does it move in 1 hour?
items.e: Step 1: 1 hr = 60 min, so 60 × 5 = 300 cm. Step 2: 1 m = 100 cm, so 300 ÷ 100 = 3 m. (300 m forgets to convert.)

items.q: A cooler holds 3 gal of water. How many 1-pint bottles can be filled from it?
items.e: 1 gal = 4 qt and 1 qt = 2 pt, so 1 gal = 8 pt. 3 × 8 = 24 bottles. (12 counts quarts, and 48 counts cups.)

items.q: A recipe uses 34 cup of milk. Maya makes 4 batches. How many pints of milk does she need?
items.e: Step 1: 4 × 34 = 124 = 3 cups. Step 2: 2 cups = 1 pt, so 3 ÷ 2 = 1 12 pt. (3 pt forgets to convert, and 6 pt multiplies by 2 instead of dividing.)

items.q: Lemonade is made with 10 qt of water and 6 pt of juice. How many gallons of lemonade is that?
items.e: Step 1: 6 pt = 6 ÷ 2 = 3 qt, so the total is 10 + 3 = 13 qt. Step 2: 4 qt = 1 gal, so 13 ÷ 4 = 3 R1 = 3 14 gal. (4 gal adds 10 + 6 without changing pints to quarts, and 13 gal forgets to change quarts to gallons.)

items.q: Ruby has a 5 m rope. She cuts off 3 pieces that are each 85 cm long. How many meters of rope are left?
items.e: Step 1: 3 × 85 = 255 cm = 2.55 m cut off. Step 2: 5 − 2.55 = 2.45 m. (2.55 m is the part cut off, 4.15 m subtracts only one piece, and 4.745 m treats 255 cm as 0.255 m.)

items.q: Luis has a 1.5 L bottle of water. He drinks 350 mL in the morning and 0.4 L in the afternoon. How many milliliters are left?
A movie is 2 14 hours long. Mia has watched 85 minutes. How many minutes are left?
items.e: Step 1: 2 14 hr = 120 + 15 = 135 min. Step 2: 135 − 85 = 50 min. (60 min reads 2 14 hr as 2 hr 25 min, and 35 min forgets the 14 hour.)

items.q: A puppy weighed 3 lb when it was born. Now it weighs 10 lb 8 oz. How many ounces has it gained?
items.e: Step 1: 10 lb 8 oz − 3 lb = 7 lb 8 oz. Step 2: 7 × 16 = 112, and 112 + 8 = 120 oz. (78 oz uses 10 ounces in a pound, and 168 oz is the puppy's weight now.)

items.q: A shelf is 3 ft long. Each book on it is 1 12 in thick. How many books fit on the shelf?
items.e: Step 1: 3 ft = 3 × 12 = 36 in. Step 2: 36 ÷ 1 12 = 24 books (2 books fill 3 inches, and 36 ÷ 3 × 2 = 24). (2 books forgets to change feet to inches, and 20 uses 10 inches in a foot.)

items.q: A baker has 3 bags of flour. Each bag holds 2.5 kg. A loaf of bread uses 500 g. How many loaves can the baker make?
items.e: Step 1: 3 × 2.5 = 7.5 kg = 7,500 g. Step 2: 7,500 ÷ 500 = 15 loaves. (5 loaves uses only 1 bag, and 150 loaves changes 7.5 kg to 75,000 g instead of 7,500 g, and 1 12 loaves changes 2.5 kg to 250 g.)

items.q: Punch is made with 1 qt of orange juice, 3 pt of apple juice and 6 cups of ginger ale. How many cups of punch is that?
items.e: Change to cups: 1 qt = 4 cups and 3 pt = 3 × 2 = 6 cups. 4 + 6 + 6 = 16 cups, which is exactly 1 gal. (10 adds the numbers without converting.)

items.q: Owen practices soccer for 1 hr 45 min, 4 days a week. How long does he practice each week?
items.e: Step 1: 1 hr 45 min = 105 min, and 4 × 105 = 420 min. Step 2: 420 ÷ 60 = 7 hr. (5.8 hr multiplies 1.45 × 4, as if an hour had 100 minutes, and 4 hr 45 min multiplies only the hours.)

items.q: A truck can carry 2 tons. Each crate weighs 250 lb. How many crates can the truck carry?
items.e: Step 1: 1 ton = 2,000 lb, so 2 tons = 4,000 lb. Step 2: 4,000 ÷ 250 = 16 crates. (8 crates uses only 1 ton, 160 crates divides by 25 instead of 250, and 500 crates multiplies 2 × 250.)

items.q: Sofia walks 14 mi to school and 14 mi back home, 5 days a week. How many feet does she walk in a week?
items.e: Step 1: 14 mi = 5,280 ÷ 4 = 1,320 ft. Step 2: each day 2 × 1,320 = 2,640 ft. Step 3: 5 × 2,640 = 13,200 ft. (6,600 ft counts only the walk to school.)

items.q: A backpack can hold 5 kg. Eli puts in 3 books of 650 g each and a laptop of 1.8 kg. How many more kilograms can the backpack hold?
items.e: Step 1: 3 × 650 = 1,950 g = 1.95 kg. Step 2: 1.95 + 1.8 = 3.75 kg in the bag. Step 3: 5 − 3.75 = 1.25 kg. (3.75 kg is what is already in the bag, and 2.55 kg counts only one book.)

items.q: Grace practices piano for 34 hr on Monday, 50 min on Tuesday and 1 14 hr on Wednesday. How many minutes is that in all?
items.e: Change to minutes: 34 hr = 45 min and 1 14 hr = 60 + 15 = 75 min. 45 + 50 + 75 = 170 min (2 hr 50 min). (250 min uses 100 minutes in an hour, and 110 min forgets the 1 in 1 14 hr.)

items.q: Kai has 4 yd of ribbon. Each bow uses 2 ft 6 in. How many whole bows can he make?
items.e: Use inches: 4 yd = 4 × 36 = 144 in and 2 ft 6 in = 30 in. 144 ÷ 30 = 4 R24, so 4 bows, with 24 in left over. (5 rounds up, but there is not enough ribbon for a 5th bow. 6 ignores the 6 inches: 12 ft ÷ 2 ft.)
